title_en: Divers Recover a Mysterious Cauldron That Had Been Hiding at the Bottom of an English River for Hundreds of Years
title_zh: 潜水员发现了一个隐藏在英国河底数百年的神秘大锅

paragraphs.en: When the divers ducked beneath the surface, they knew their target: a mysterious iron cauldron at the bottom of England’s River Wear. They had no idea how the vessel had ended up there, though they were fairly certain it had been underwater for hundreds of years. Their mission was to recover it from the watery darkness and bring it back to the surface.
paragraphs.zh: 当潜水员潜入水面之下时，他们清楚自己的目标：英格兰威尔河（River Wear）河底一口神秘的铁锅。他们不知道这口锅是如何到了那里，尽管他们相当确定它已在水下埋藏了数百年。他们的任务是将它从幽暗的水中打捞出来，带回水面。

paragraphs.en: The operation unfolded “like clockwork,” Gary Bankhead , an underwater archaeologist at England’s Durham University, tells the Northern Echo ’s Andrew White. “It was very much like a military operation. Everybody had a specific job.”
paragraphs.zh: 英格兰杜伦大学（Durham University）的水下考古学家加里·班克黑德（Gary Bankhead）告诉《北方回声报》（Northern Echo）的安德鲁·怀特（Andrew White），整个行动“像钟表一样”精准展开。“这非常像一次军事行动。每个人都有明确的任务。”

paragraphs.en: After freeing the artifact from debris, the divers secured it in thick green netting inside a metal cage. Team members on a recovery craft above then slowly pulled it up into the late morning sun. It arrived back on land for the first time in centuries—but just how much time had passed?
paragraphs.zh: 潜水员将这件文物从杂物中清理出来后，把它固定在金属笼内厚厚的绿色网中。上方打捞船上的队员随后缓缓将其拉起，升入临近正午的阳光中。这口锅数百年来首次回到陆地——但究竟过去了多少年？

paragraphs.en: Researchers have a few loose theories. The three-legged cauldron was found alongside a trove of ancient Roman artifacts, but its design isn’t consistent with the Roman era. Experts’ best guess is that it’s medieval. Their second-best guess is that it dates to the Iron Age.
paragraphs.zh: 研究人员有几种尚无定论的说法。这口三足锅与一批古罗马文物一同被发现，但其设计风格与罗马时代不符。专家最合理的推测是它属于中世纪，其次的推测是它可追溯至铁器时代。

paragraphs.en: The Wear is located near the city of Sunderland in northern England. In recent years, volunteers investigating the riverbank have discovered roughly 800 Roman whetstones , which soldiers used to sharpen swords and other tools in antiquity, as well as coins and stone anchors .
paragraphs.zh: 威尔河位于英格兰北部的桑德兰市（Sunderland）附近。近年来，在河岸进行调查的志愿者发现了大约800块罗马磨刀石——古代士兵用来磨利刀剑和其他工具——以及硬币和石锚。

paragraphs.en: Researchers analyzed the sediment layer the whetstones were found in to determine their age, according to a statement from Durham University. The sediment samples dated to between 104 and 238 C.E.
paragraphs.zh: 根据杜伦大学的一份声明，研究人员分析了磨刀石所在沉积层以确定其年代。沉积样本的年代在公元104年至238年之间。

paragraphs.en: Researchers think the site was home to a factory that operated thousands of years ago . England was a Roman province for hundreds of years, beginning in the first century C.E., but Roman-era discoveries are rare in Sunderland. “It is only ten miles or so south of Hadrian’s Wall , so you would expect the Romans to be in Sunderland,” Bankhead told the Guardian ’s Mark Brown earlier this year. “But there has been virtually no archaeological evidence.”
paragraphs.zh: 研究人员认为，该遗址曾是数千年前一座工厂的所在地。从公元一世纪起，英格兰作为罗马行省长达数百年，但罗马时代的发现在桑德兰却很罕见。“这里距离哈德良长城（Hadrian's Wall）以南仅十英里左右，所以你会以为罗马人曾在桑德兰活动，”班克黑德今年早些时候告诉《卫报》（The Guardian）的马克·布朗（Mark Brown），“但几乎没有考古证据。”

paragraphs.en: Bankhead serves as president of the local Vedra Hylton Community Association , which has been leading the recent excavations. He spotted the cauldron while diving in the river in September 2025.
paragraphs.zh: 班克黑德是当地维德拉·希尔顿社区协会（Vedra Hylton Community Association）的主席，该协会一直主导近期的发掘工作。2025年9月，他在河中潜水时发现了这口锅。

paragraphs.en: Bankhead estimated that the vessel weighed nearly 70 pounds —too heavy for any one diver to lift from the riverbed. For months, he and his colleagues plotted out how they would raise the cauldron safely from the river.
paragraphs.zh: 班克黑德估计这口锅重近70磅——对任何一名潜水员来说都太重，无法独自从河床抬起。数月来，他和同事们规划了如何将这口锅安全地从河中打捞上来。

paragraphs.en: That day arrived earlier this month. When the cauldron emerged from the water, Bankhead was “blown away” by its scale, as he tells BBC News ’ Pamela Bilalova. “I’d seen it previously underwater, and I estimated how big it was, but when you see it in the daylight, you just marvel at its sheer size.”
paragraphs.zh: 这一天在本月早些时候到来了。当这口锅从水中露出时，班克黑德对其规模感到“震惊”，他告诉BBC新闻（BBC News）的帕梅拉·比拉洛娃（Pamela Bilalova）。“我之前在水下见过它，也估算过它的大小，但当你白天看到它时，你会惊叹于它纯粹的尺寸。”
